record.paper_title: Hadronic production of η–mesons: recent results and open questions
record.original_question: How do a loosely bound eta-nucleon molecular interpretation and a compact quark-state interpretation of S11(1535) behave differently when additional baryons are present, and can a systematic theoretical approach be developed for eta-deuteron and eta-helium-3 systems that uses those differences to test the nature of S11(1535)?

evidence.quote: In addition, it is expected that a (loosely bound) molecule and a compact quark state behave very different in the presence of additional baryons.
This field is unfortunately still lacking a systematic approach at present, although microscopic calculations are available for both the ηd [26] and the η3He [27] system.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nucleon resonance S11(1535), a spin-1/2, isospin-1/2, negative-parity baryon resonance lying close to and strongly coupled to the eta-nucleon (ηN) channel. Two competing pictures of its internal structure are:

(i) a loosely bound ηN (and KΛ, KΣ) hadronic "molecule," generated dynamically as a quasi-bound state of meson–baryon channels by coupled-channel hadronic interactions; and

(ii) a compact three-quark (or genuine quark-model) excited baryon state of small spatial extent.

In the single-nucleon sector the two pictures can be tuned to reproduce essentially the same ηN scattering amplitude near threshold and the same pole position, so they are difficult to distinguish from πN → ηN and γN → ηN data alone. However, in environments containing additional baryons the two pictures are expected to behave differently: a loosely bound molecule should be substantially modified (e.g., Pauli blocking of its nucleon component, dispersive effects on its meson component, level rearrangement) when embedded in a few-nucleon system, whereas a compact quark state should be comparatively inert and behave more like a point-like resonance whose properties are dressed only by standard nuclear medium effects.

Problem. Develop a systematic theoretical framework for the η-deuteron (ηd) and η-helium-3 (η³He) systems that:

(a) treats the η meson, the nucleons, and the S11(1535) resonance as explicit degrees of freedom, and incorporates both structural hypotheses (i) and (ii) for S11(1535) on an equal footing within the same few-body scattering formalism (e.g., Faddeev/Faddeev–Yakubovsky or AGS-type equations with a coupled ηN–πN–S11 subsystem);

(b) yields predictions for low-energy ηd and η³He observables — including the complex η-nucleus scattering lengths, near-threshold elastic and inelastic cross sections, possible quasi-bound or virtual η-mesic states, and the energy dependence of the production amplitudes near threshold — as functions of which hypothesis (i) or (ii) is adopted for S11(1535);

(c) identifies observables in ηd and η³He for which the molecule and compact-quark interpretations give quantitatively or qualitatively distinguishable predictions, thereby providing experimentally accessible tests of the nature of S11(1535).

Construct such a framework and determine whether the resulting differences between the two interpretations are large enough, given current and foreseeable experimental precision, to discriminate between them.
artifact.category_tag: eta-mesic few-body systems and baryon resonance structure
artifact.status_search_result: Reviews of η-mesic nuclei (including recent surveys of η-³He bound-state searches) confirm that the structure of S11(1535) — molecular vs. compact quark state — is still an unsettled issue, and that while individual microscopic ηd and η³He calculations exist, a unified systematic few-body framework that exploits the molecule-vs-quark-state distinction to test S11(1535) has not been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Status of the Search for η-Mesic Nuclei with Particular Focus on η-Helium Bound States
status_evidence.snippet: Review discusses N*(1535) as key ingredient in eta-mesic nucleus formation and notes ongoing uncertainties about the underlying eta-nucleon interaction.
status_evidence.claim: The nature of S11(1535) and its role in η-nucleus dynamics remain active open issues.

status_evidence.title: Study of the N* momentum distribution for experimental η-mesic 3He searches
status_evidence.snippet: Recent calculations probe N*(1535) properties in η-³He but do not unify molecular and quark-state pictures within a common few-body framework.
status_evidence.claim: Microscopic ηd and η³He calculations exist, but a systematic framework distinguishing the two S11(1535) interpretations has not been built.
